whatWasChecked: two residual failure paths in the latest cleanup helper, identified by source review and reproduced against the committed baseline code before any edit

defects.title: depth-limit exhaustion did not fail closed
defects.observedBaseline: a directory chain deeper than the bound was silently skipped: enumerateLinks returned ok:true with 0 links while a junction existed below the boundary; the caller received no signal to stop
defects.measurementMethod: disposable directory tree under the system temp root with a junction placed below the depth bound
defects.patch: a named DEPTH_LIMIT_EXCEEDED condition is recorded when a further directory would require descending beyond the bound; enumerateLinks returns ok:false; destroyDisposableCheckout blocks with ENUMERATION_COMPLETE:false before the Git removal decision and preserves the tree
defects.positiveControl: S1-A: the over-deep tree inside an owned checkout yields CLEANUP_BLOCKED, ENUMERATION_COMPLETE:false, DEPTH_LIMIT_EXCEEDED:true, gitWorktreeRemoveForceExecuted:false, recursiveRemoveExecuted:false, worktreePreserved:true
defects.negativeControl: S1-A-DEFECT_PRESENT (C1): the same tree on the unpatched helper yielded ok:true and 0 links
defects.operationCallHistory: the injected filesystem adapter recorded no removeTree call and the injected Git adapter recorded no removeWorktreeForce call

defects.title: deletion aftermath confused ENOENT with inspection failure
defects.baselineLocation: scripts/r3l0ciarlcfsh/safe-cleanup.mjs realFilesystemAdapter().exists() and the post-Git-removal branch reading fs.exists(resolvedRoot) !== true
defects.observedBaseline: exists() swallowed every lstat error into false; with Git removal returning without removing and postflight inspection failing with EPERM/EACCES, the helper reported CLEANED / worktreeRemoved:true / destructiveFallbackExecuted:true while the directory was physically still on disk
defects.measurementMethod: owned disposable checkout with a fault-injected adapter reporting a permission error on the root path and a Git adapter that returns without removing
defects.patch: realFilesystemAdapter() gains an error-aware inspect(); classifyRemovalState() reports REMOVED_CONFIRMED only on ENOENT, STILL_PRESENT when present, STATE_UNKNOWN otherwise; the Git error and filesystem observation are carried as diagnostics; exists() is no longer the sole witness and CLEANED is never reported when the state is unknown
positiveControls: S1-B1 Git throws + present -> STILL_PRESENT blocked
S1-B2 Git throws + EPERM -> STATE_UNKNOWN blocked
S1-B2b classifier fallback (no inspect) + EPERM -> STATE_UNKNOWN
S1-B3 Git returns + EACCES -> STATE_UNKNOWN blocked
S1-B4 Git returns + ENOENT -> REMOVED_CONFIRMED -> CLEANED
S1-B5 Git returns + present -> STILL_PRESENT blocked
S1-B6 no failure branch invokes a recursive removal
defects.negativeControl: S1-B-DEFECT_PRESENT (C1): the unpatched helper reported CLEANED while the directory remained on disk
defects.operationCallHistory: the injected filesystem adapter recorded no removeTree call in any blocked branch; the injected Git adapter recorded removeWorktreeForce only in the S1-B4 success branch

threatModelExclusions: an adversarial process able to modify arbitrary filesystem entries concurrently with the cleanup (not addressed, not tested)
a platform whose reparse-point semantics differ from the ones measured on this host
evidenceLevel: T2 (real filesystem operations on disposable directories under the system temp root, with fault-injected adapters for the dangerous branches)
law: both corrections are bounded to the latest cleanup helper; every dangerous branch is measured through the real control flow with a fault-injected adapter, and no helper boolean stands in for proof that an operation ran
